page.overview:
Who is Arkansaurus?

("Arkansas lizard") is a genus of ornithomimid theropod dinosaur that was discovered in Lockesburg, Arkansas (USA), living during the Early Cretaceous. Only one species is known: A. fridayi. Its nearest relative is , who also happens to live in the United States. It is named for the state it was found as well as its discoverer J.B. Friday, who found the dinosaur's fossilized foot on his farm in 1972. Arkansaurus was declared the official state dinosaur of Arkansas in 2017. Interestingly, the scientific name was coined in 1977, but would be officially described in 2018. In the meantime, it was declared a nomen dubium.

Arkansaurus fossils come from the Trinity Group, which was home to other dinosaurs such as Acrocanthosaurus - the apex predator of the region - and the giant sauropod Sauroposeidon.

Arkansaurus was illustrated by Timothy Bradley in the Dinopedia section of Jurassic Park Institute, depicted for some reason as a carcharodontosaurid rather than an ornithomimid. Nevertheless, it hasn't received a dino card before its closure in 2006.
